## Role and Accounting Boundary

This page defines the turbine electrical output used to compare electricity
export, centralised hydrogen and decentralised hydrogen. The adopted model
boundary is the **AC output of the grid-side inverter, before the step-up
transformer**. The generator and generator-side rectifier remain common to all
cases; their costs and losses are not removed when comparing architectures.

The transformer is outside the turbine **cost and power-output boundary** used
here. It is usually housed inside the turbine, in the tower or nacelle, but
physical location does not determine cost ownership [@bvg2019OffshoreGuide].
Its purchase cost and downstream losses belong to electrical infrastructure;
its mass still belongs in the applicable supported-mass and lifting inventory.

## Single-Line Diagram

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  subgraph turbine["Turbine accounting scope"]
    G["Generator"] --> R["Rectifier"]
    R --> D["DC link"]
    D --> I["Grid-side inverter"]
  end
  I --> B["Power-curve boundary: inverter AC output / transformer LV side"]
  B --> T["Step-up transformer: electrical-infrastructure scope; usually housed in turbine"]
  T --> A["Infield AC grid"]
  D -. "Decentralised alternative: inverter and transformer omitted" .-> H["Electrolyser interface: direct DC or dedicated DC/DC"]
```

The DC branch replaces the AC path; it is not an additional simultaneous export
path. “LV side” identifies the lower-voltage transformer winding relative to the
infield grid; it does not prescribe a particular equipment voltage class.

## Power Available to Each Architecture

Required inputs are the turbine power curve at the declared boundary and the
inverter and transformer efficiencies. Their specifications and evidence belong
to [Power Conversion Equipment](../electrical_infra/power_conversion_equipment.qmd#sec-grid-side-inverter).
No numerical efficiency is independently defined on this page.

For electricity export and centralised hydrogen, the power delivered to the
infield grid is:

$$
P_{\mathrm{array,in}}=P_{\mathrm{curve}}\eta_{\mathrm{tr}}.
$$

For decentralised hydrogen, removing the inverter recovers its conversion loss:

$$
P_{\mathrm{DC}}=\frac{P_{\mathrm{curve}}}{\eta_{\mathrm{inv}}},
\qquad
\Delta P_{\mathrm{inv}}=P_{\mathrm{curve}}
\left(\frac{1}{\eta_{\mathrm{inv}}}-1\right).
$$

Here $P_{\mathrm{curve}}$ is inverter AC output, $P_{\mathrm{array,in}}$ is
transformer output, $P_{\mathrm{DC}}$ is available DC-link power and
$\Delta P_{\mathrm{inv}}$ is recovered inverter loss, all in kW.
$\eta_{\mathrm{inv}}$ and $\eta_{\mathrm{tr}}$ are dimensionless output/input
efficiencies at the applicable operating point. Division reverses the inverter
loss; adding a loss percentage is not equivalent. These expressions assume
the same upstream operating point and do not authorise operation beyond the
generator, rectifier or DC interface ratings.

The [DC Integration](../hydrogen_production/dc_integration.qmd#sec-dc-compared-cases)
page defines the direct connection of the electrolyser to the DC link and its
matching and protection conditions. The conservative alternative retains a
dedicated stack-side DC/DC converter. In either case, retained interface losses
are applied after recovering inverter losses. Neither architecture receives a
generator or rectifier efficiency credit.

## Cost Boundary

For comparable per-turbine supply costs in EUR2025, let
$C_{\mathrm{legacy}}$ denote a conventional turbine package that includes the
transformer, $C_{\mathrm{tr}}$ its consistently allocated transformer cost, and
$C_{\mathrm{inv}}$ the separable grid-side inverter cost. Then:

$$
C_{\mathrm{turbine,AC}}=C_{\mathrm{legacy}}-C_{\mathrm{tr}},
\qquad
C_{\mathrm{turbine,DC}}=C_{\mathrm{turbine,AC}}-C_{\mathrm{inv}}.
$$

The AC architectures book $C_{\mathrm{tr}}$ once under electrical infrastructure.
The decentralised architecture does not purchase it. Added DC/DC equipment and
changes to protection, cooling and cabling are separate retained costs, not part
of the inverter credit. An unknown inverter price is not a zero price.

The [turbine cost ledger](wind_turbine.qmd#sec-turbine-electrical-credit) derives
the conventional package including its transformer, then allocates that same
calibrated transformer term to electrical infrastructure in AC cases. The
combined AC supply cost is preserved. No inverter cost credit is claimed.

## Reference-Curve and Implementation Status

The inverter-output boundary above is the adopted model convention, not a claim
that every published turbine curve uses the same measurement point. A curve
must identify whether converter and transformer losses are already included.

**Article source boundary confirmed.** On 9 October 2026 the user confirmed that
the supplied [article curve](../research_articles/turbine_level_hydrogen/reference_case.qmd)
is measured after the inverter and before the transformer. Numerical curve and
operating-state values are unchanged. The earlier generator-output description
has been corrected; this confirmation is distinct from independent source validation.

**Implementation and remaining numerical adoption.** The model implements
inverter-loss recovery, downstream transformer loss and transformer cost
reallocation. Inverter-only and transformer efficiencies are provisional
user-approved assumptions, with reference/validation TODOs on
[Power Conversion Equipment](../electrical_infra/power_conversion_equipment.qmd).
These assumptions permit screening runs but are not measured specifications.
No generator or rectifier losses are added again.
